collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: I keep losing patients after hours
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: losing patients after hours,calls going straight to voicemail after hours,missing about 20 calls a week

transcript:
User: Hi — I saw your ad on Facebook about answering missed calls. I keep losing patients after hours, so I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Got it, losing patients after hours is painful — and yeah, that’s exactly what we focus on.  

So, when someone calls your office after you’re closed right now, what actually happens to that call — straight to voicemail, an answering service, or something else?
User: Right now, calls go straight to voicemail after hours. We miss about 20 calls a week this way.
Agent: Yeah, that adds up fast — 20 people a week hitting voicemail after hours is a lot.  

Those patients who call and hit voicemail… do they usually end up calling you back later, or do you feel like most of them just move on to another practice?
User: Most of them probably move on to another practice, which is why I'm interested in this service.
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — if they’re calling after hours, they usually need help now, not tomorrow.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what those 20 missed calls a week might actually be costing you in lost treatment revenue?
User: Not exactly, but I estimate half would book if answered, with an average appointment value of $650.
Agent: So with your numbers, even just catching half of those 20 missed calls, that’s about $6,500 walking out the door every week in lost treatment.  

When you hear that, does it feel about right for your practice, or does it seem high/low to you?
User: That sounds about right, considering what I've seen with our missed call volume and potential bookings.
Agent: Yeah, that lines up — with your numbers, we’re looking at roughly $28,000 a month tied to those after-hours voicemails.  

So, what we do is have every missed call automatically answered right away by our system, it talks to the patient in natural language, books the appointment (or takes a detailed message), and sends everything straight to your team — what part of that are you most interested in: actually booking the after-hours patients, or just making sure no call ever dies in voicemail?
User: I'm most interested in booking after-hours patients to prevent them from going elsewhere.
Agent: Makes total sense — if they’re in pain at 7pm and you can book them, you keep that patient instead of the ER or another practice.  

So, this is exactly what we walk through on a quick live call — we plug in your numbers, show you how the system books those after-hours patients for you, and what that $28k/month could look like recovered; would you be open to a 20‑minute walkthrough sometime this week?
User: Yes, please book the live call for a walkthrough this week. Tomorrow afternoon works for me.
Agent: Perfect, we can definitely set that up for you.  

To get this booked, what’s your first name?
User: My first name is Maria.
Agent: Nice to meet you, Maria.  

And your last name?
User: My last name is Gonzales.
Agent: Got it, Maria Gonzales.  

And what’s the name of your practice?
User: The name of my practice is Bright Smile Dental.
Agent: Bright Smile Dental — got it.  

And is the number you’re calling from right now the best number to reach you for the walkthrough?
Agent: Perfect, we’ll use this number.  

Quick check — are you on Central time?
User: Yes, the best contact number for me is +13125551234.
Agent: Perfect, thanks Maria.  

Tomorrow afternoon I can get you in as soon as 12:15 or 2:30 Central — which works better for you?
User: Let's book the live call for 2:30 Central tomorrow.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that on our calendar for tomorrow at 2:30 Central.
Agent: Awesome — you’re all set for tomorrow at 2:30 Central with Jay to walk through how we can book those after-hours patients for Bright Smile Dental. You’ll get a text with the confirmation and a link in case you ever need to reschedule. Really glad you reached out, Maria — have a great rest of your day, and we’ll talk tomorrow!
